name: Namibia

facts.languages: Afrikaans, German, English, Herero, Khoekhoe, Kwangali, Lozi, Ndonga, Tswana

snapshot: A stable, sparsely populated democracy that elected its first woman president in 2024 and hopes new offshore oil and green hydrogen will tackle deep inequality.
culture: Namibia's peoples include the Ovambo, the largest group, and Herero, Nama, Damara and San, alongside German- and Afrikaans-speaking minorities, reflecting German and South African rule. Herero women's Victorian-style dresses and horned hats are a living reminder of colonial history. The Namib, the world's oldest desert, and Etosha's wildlife are major attractions.
society: Namibia has one of the world's highest levels of inequality, rooted in land dispossession; most commercial farmland is still owned by a white minority. Mining of diamonds and uranium drives exports. Germany acknowledged in 2021 that its killing of Herero and Nama people in 1904 to 1908 was genocide, but descendants rejected the reparations offered.
situation: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah of SWAPO, the liberation movement in power since independence in 1990, won the November 2024 election with 58 percent and became Namibia's first woman president in March 2025. Big offshore oil discoveries by Shell and TotalEnergies have raised hopes of new wealth.
power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected for five years, at most two terms, and heads the government alongside a prime minister; SWAPO has won every election since independence in 1990.
